clue.text: Pick up line provided by team's leader

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for line
'provided' as in 'provided that' means if

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word before it is kept

parts.note: first letter of team

explanation.surface: A coach scribbles down a play, picked up from what the captain says.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to raise it, a direct synonym of the phrasal verb meaning raise.

clue.text: Type of printer that's turned up in fire sale

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the letters are sitting inside the following phrase, running across its word break

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A cheap printer is spotted among the bargains at a fire-damage sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser printer is a common kind of office printer that fuses toner using a beam of light.

clue.text: At sea, fault inelegant aide-de-camp

indicators.note: something at sea is confused and adrift, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A naval aide is criticised for being clumsy while serving on board ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag lieutenant is the naval officer serving as personal assistant to an admiral, the navy's equivalent of an aide-de-camp.

clue.text: Vehicle with particular floor covering

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a pet subject or pet project is one's particular favourite

explanation.surface: A car comes fitted with the owner's choice of mat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' is used in the sense of a favourite, as in a pet hate.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet is a thick woven fabric laid over a room's floor.

clue.text: Mobile busy?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: able to move about, not bedridden
second meaning: occupied, doing a lot

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests asking whether a mobile phone line is engaged; the two words are separate senses of one adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An active patient is up and moving, and an active person is energetically occupied.

clue.text: Accommodate person of great patience in a fix

parts.note: to put someone up is to give them a bed
the biblical Job is proverbial for patience

explanation.surface: Someone saintly agrees to host a guest who is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a fix' reads as being in trouble, but 'a fix' is the definition and 'in' only joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-up job is a rigged or prearranged affair, which is what a fix means.

clue.text: Body temperature, approximately

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
'or so' means approximately, as in ten or so

explanation.surface: A doctor gives a rough reading of a patient's body temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Declared policy from rostrum

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a party's stated programme
second meaning: a raised stage for speakers

explanation.surface: A politician announces policy while standing on the speaker's stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A political platform is a published set of policies, and a platform is also a raised stage a speaker addresses a crowd from.

clue.text: Time to fulfil one's obligations in any foreign dock after repair

indicators.note: repairing something takes it apart and puts it back together differently

parts.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A ship's bills fall due in whatever overseas port it puts into for repairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of the fodder, but it is the link; only the three words after it are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The day of reckoning is the moment when debts must be settled or one must answer for one's actions.

clue.text: English poet, one avoiding stress round New York

indicators.note: going round means the remaining word wraps around the next piece
to avoid something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: tension is stress or strain
one as the Roman numeral I, the letter removed
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An English poet tries to stay relaxed while visiting New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of TENSION and put NY into the middle of what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate born in Lincolnshire.

clue.text: Young actress the Spanish upset during opening

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of another

parts.note: the start is the opening

indicators.note: upset means tipped over, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A young actress from Spain is upset on her opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: A starlet is a young actress being promoted as a future star.

clue.text: Row of houses — create changes involving first in row

indicators.note: the word changes its form, so its letters are rearranged
involving brings the extra letter into the mix before the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first in means only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: first letter of the final word of the clue

explanation.surface: A developer builds a terrace by altering the first house in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a continuous row of joined houses, a common British street layout.

clue.text: Who, say, could be in favour of sister accepting ring offered by brother, perhaps?

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a brother is one example of a relative
pro means for or in favour of
a nun is called Sister
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: Someone wonders who would back a sister taking a ring her brother offers.
explanation.walkthrough: RELATIVE comes first in the answer though its words end the clue; 'offered by' only places it. NUN takes in O to make NOUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Who is an example of a relative pronoun, one that introduces a relative clause.

clue.text: Market town in Britain, once desecrated

parts.note: BR is an abbreviation for Britain

indicators.note: something desecrated has been violated and wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A British market town whose old church was once desecrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Britain' looks like part of the definition, but 'in' is the link and Britain is wordplay. BRECON is a market town in mid-Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Brecon is a small Welsh market town in the Brecon Beacons area of Powys.

clue.text: Unpleasant around river crossing industrial city

indicators.note: around means one word encloses the next item

parts.note: bad means unpleasant
R is the abbreviation for river
a ford is a shallow river crossing

explanation.surface: A grim river crossing in an industrial city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradford is a West Yorkshire city that grew on the wool industry.

clue.text: Type of pate that may be got from goose fair (not duck)

indicators.note: getting something from material means working it up into a new form
not means without, so the following item is removed

parts.note: taken as written
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O

explanation.surface: A goose-based pate might be on sale at Nottingham's Goose Fair, so long as there's no duck.
explanation.walkthrough: Goose Fair is a traditional autumn fair in Nottingham. A duck is a cricket score of nought, so one O goes before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Foie gras is a rich pate of fattened goose or duck liver.

clue.text: Use train

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a right or power is to use it
second meaning: to drill or work out

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns, but each is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: One exercises an option by using it, and exercising is physical training.

clue.text: Police unit manhandled ten after fashionable event

parts.note: in means in fashion

indicators.note: roughly manhandled things get pushed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
taken as written

explanation.surface: Detectives rough up ten people outside a trendy venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the police unit and the rearranged number follow the word for fashionable, though the clue lists them first. The CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident is an occurrence or happening, a synonym of event.

clue.text: I'm stopping boy identifying an element

indicators.note: something stopping a gap sits inside it, plugging it

parts.note: Antony is a boy's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stops a boy to identify a chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An' looks like wordplay, but it belongs to the definition; the boy's name supplies those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a metalloid chemical element, symbol Sb.

clue.text: Watch fire in western half of Bucks town

indicators.note: in an across entry the western half is the left-hand portion, so the rest of the word is dropped

parts.note: a town in Buckinghamshire

explanation.surface: A lookout's fire burns in the west of a Buckinghamshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county; Beaconsfield is one of its towns, and its first six letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal fire lit on a hill to give warning, which a watch would keep.

clue.text: Urge almost gone over drink

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them

indicators.note: turned over, in a down entry, means read upwards
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says the urge to drink has nearly passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a drink of beaten eggs, milk and sugar, often with spirits.

clue.text: Stopping train for girls' college

parts.note: finishing means stopping
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A railway announcement that a train terminates for a girls' college.
explanation.definitionFit: A finishing school is a private college teaching young women social graces.

clue.text: Chide son, lacking in affection

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
cold means unaffectionate

explanation.surface: A parent tells off a son who shows no warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold is to rebuke someone angrily, the same as to chide.

clue.text: Generous lager poured out

indicators.note: poured out suggests spilling, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A barman pours a generous measure of lager.
explanation.definitionFit: A large helping is a generous one, a direct synonym.

clue.text: British writer published quite a few

parts.note: a newspaper ran a story when it published it
some means a fair number

explanation.surface: A British author has had a fair number of books published.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome was the British author of the Swallows and Amazons children's books.

clue.text: Bridge player leads as row becomes more unpleasant

parts.note: North is one of the four players at bridge
taken as written
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A bridge player takes the lead as an argument turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line of seats. 'Leads' puts the player first.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, meaning more unpleasant.

clue.text: Senility demonstrated by magistrate imprisoning volunteers

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding something inside, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of Venice
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An aged magistrate shows his senility by locking up volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was the British army's part-time volunteer force.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the period of feeble-minded old age, which senility describes.

clue.text: Try reflecting about giant

indicators.note: a mirror reflection runs the opposite way, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: to have a go is to try
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone tries to think carefully about a giant.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant in folklore and fairy tales.
